{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01N95U97RrFW32tG2R9XMCn6","type":"tool_result","content":"=== sources/full_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\n# The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a\n# passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh\n=== sources/run_conformance.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n=== sources/setup_harness.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.\n#\n# Requires network access and a Go toolchain of at least 1.22 — the same floor\n# stack/go.md sets for the deliverable. The Go shipped by apt on Debian and\n# Ubuntu is frequently older and will fail; install the official tarball instead:\n#\n#     curl -sL https://go.dev/dl/go1.24.6.linux-amd64.tar.gz -o go.tgz\n#     sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go.tgz\n#     export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sh sources/setup_harness.sh              # install to $HOME/.local/bin\n#   GOBIN=/usr/local/bin sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nset -eu\n\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=v2.2.0\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}\"\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"error: no go toolchain on PATH; see the header of this script\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"go:      $(go version)\"\necho \"target:  ${GOBIN}/toml-test\"\necho \"version: ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${GOBIN}\"\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN}\" go install \\\n    \"github.com/toml-lang/toml-test/v2/cmd/toml-test@${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\necho\n\"${GOBIN}/toml-test\" version\n\ncase \":${PATH}:\" in\n    *\":${GOBIN}:\"*) ;;\n    *) echo\n       echo \"warning: ${GOBIN} is not on PATH. Add it, or export\"\n       echo \"         TOML_TEST=${GOBIN}/toml-test before running the suite.\" ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_contract.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_contract.sh — governed gates for boundaries not represented by one toml-test slice.\nset -eu\n\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_contract.sh <architecture|decoder>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\n\ncase \"$1\" in\n  architecture)\n    test -f go.mod\n    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then\n      echo \"go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    ;;\n  decoder)\n    go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    stage_dir=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    trap 'rm -rf \"$stage_dir\"' EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n    printf 'answer = 42\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/valid.json\" 2>\"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    python - \"$stage_dir/valid.json\" <<'PY'\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nwith open(sys.argv[1], encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n    decoded = json.load(stream)\nassert decoded == {\"answer\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"42\"}}\nPY\n\n    if printf 'answer = [\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/invalid.out\" 2>\"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"; then\n      echo \"malformed TOML exited successfully\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.out\"\n    test -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"\n    ;;\n  *)\n    echo \"unknown stage contract: $1\" >&2\n    exit 2\n    ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.\n#\n# Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder,\n# then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1. Exit status is the\n# verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\n# The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a\n# passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh\n=== sources/run_conformance.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n=== sources/setup_harness.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.\n#\n# Requires network access and a Go toolchain of at least 1.22 — the same floor\n# stack/go.md sets for the deliverable. The Go shipped by apt on Debian and\n# Ubuntu is frequently older and will fail; install the official tarball instead:\n#\n#     curl -sL https://go.dev/dl/go1.24.6.linux-amd64.tar.gz -o go.tgz\n#     sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go.tgz\n#     export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sh sources/setup_harness.sh              # install to $HOME/.local/bin\n#   GOBIN=/usr/local/bin sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nset -eu\n\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=v2.2.0\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}\"\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"error: no go toolchain on PATH; see the header of this script\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"go:      $(go version)\"\necho \"target:  ${GOBIN}/toml-test\"\necho \"version: ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${GOBIN}\"\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN}\" go install \\\n    \"github.com/toml-lang/toml-test/v2/cmd/toml-test@${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\necho\n\"${GOBIN}/toml-test\" version\n\ncase \":${PATH}:\" in\n    *\":${GOBIN}:\"*) ;;\n    *) echo\n       echo \"warning: ${GOBIN} is not on PATH. Add it, or export\"\n       echo \"         TOML_TEST=${GOBIN}/toml-test before running the suite.\" ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_contract.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_contract.sh — governed gates for boundaries not represented by one toml-test slice.\nset -eu\n\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_contract.sh <architecture|decoder>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\n\ncase \"$1\" in\n  architecture)\n    test -f go.mod\n    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then\n      echo \"go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    ;;\n  decoder)\n    go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    stage_dir=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    trap 'rm -rf \"$stage_dir\"' EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n    printf 'answer = 42\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/valid.json\" 2>\"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    python - \"$stage_dir/valid.json\" <<'PY'\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nwith open(sys.argv[1], encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n    decoded = json.load(stream)\nassert decoded == {\"answer\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"42\"}}\nPY\n\n    if printf 'answer = [\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/invalid.out\" 2>\"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"; then\n      echo \"malformed TOML exited successfully\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.out\"\n    test -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"\n    ;;\n  *)\n    echo \"unknown stage contract: $1\" >&2\n    exit 2\n    ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.\n#\n# Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder,\n# then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1. Exit status is the\n# verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run \"$1\"","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01N95U97RrFW32tG2R9XMCn6","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '_'\n}\n\n// isDisallowedControl reports whether c is a control character TOML forbids in\n// strings and comments. Tab is the only control character it allows. Line breaks\n// are excluded here because each caller decides whether a line break is legal.\nfunc isDisallowedControl(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c < 0x20 && c != '\\t' && c != '\\n') || c == 0x7f\n}\npackage toml\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. A nested table\n// is a table value; a key/value pair is the tagged map[string]any that value returns.\n// The two dynamic types differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table map[string]any\n\n// key reads a dotted key: one or more key parts joined by '.'. Spaces and tabs around\n// each part are ignored. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key. Table headers are not\n// decoded yet, so a '[' is reported as a syntax error by the caller.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below doc, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(doc table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tcur := doc\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, exists := cur[part]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tsub := table{}\n\t\t\tcur[part] = sub\n\t\t\tcur = sub\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsub, ok := next.(table)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", part)\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = sub\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps for the caller. Values are shared,\n// not copied, because each leaf is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t))\n\tfor k, v := range t {\n\t\tif sub, ok := v.(table); ok {\n\t\t\tout[k] = sub.export()\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n// Command toml-decoder reads a TOML document on stdin and writes its\n// tagged-JSON description to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr and malformed\n// input exits non-zero.\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"os\"\n\n\t\"github.com/owner/toml-decoder/internal/toml\"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tif err := run(os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, \"toml-decoder:\", err)\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n\n// run decodes the document on in and encodes the result as JSON to out.\nfunc run(in io.Reader, out io.Writer) error {\n\tdoc, err := toml.Decode(in)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"decode: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn json.NewEncoder(out).Encode(doc)\n}","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01CWDZnWRfEBip175UkTYAtU","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01J5aLBHzBhcn8GtTXMpbrNn","type":"tool_result","content":"=== array-implicit\n# This test is a bit tricky. It should fail because the first use of\n# `[[albums.songs]]` without first declaring `albums` implies that `albums`\n# must be a table. The alternative would be quite weird. Namely, it wouldn't\n# comply with the TOML spec: \"Each double-bracketed sub-table will belong to \n# the most *recently* defined table element *above* it.\"\n#\n# This is in contrast to the *valid* test, table-array-implicit where\n# `[[albums.songs]]` works by itself, so long as `[[albums]]` isn't declared\n# later. (Although, `[albums]` could be.)\n[[albums.songs]]\nname = \"Glory Days\"\n\n[[albums]]\nname = \"Born in the USA\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-01\n# First a.b.c defines a table: a.b.c = {z=9}\n#\n# Then we define a.b.c.t = \"str\" to add a str to the above table, making it:\n#\n#   a.b.c = {z=9, t=\"...\"}\n#\n# While this makes sense, logically, it was decided this is not valid TOML as\n# it's too confusing/convoluted.\n# \n# See: https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/issues/846\n#      https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/pull/859\n\n[a.b.c]\n  z = 9\n\n[a]\n  b.c.t = \"Using dotted keys to add to [a.b.c] after explicitly defining it above is not allowed\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-02\n# This is the same issue as in injection-1.toml, except that nests one level\n# deeper. See that file for a more complete description.\n\n[a.b.c.d]\n  z = 9\n\n[a]\n  b.c.d.k.t = \"Using dotted keys to add to [a.b.c.d] after explicitly defining it above is not allowed\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-03\n[[a.b]]\n\n[a]\nb.y = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-04\n[dependencies.foo]\nversion = \"0.16\"\n\n[dependencies]\nlibc = \"0.2\"\n\n[dependencies]\nrand = \"0.3.14\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-05\na.b.c = 1\na.b = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-06\na = 1\na.b = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-07\na = {k1 = 1, k1.name = \"joe\"}\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-08\n[a.b.c]\nz = 9\n\n[[totally_unrelated]]\nx = 123\n\n[a]\nb.c.t = \"this should NOT be allowed\"\n=== overwrite-with-deep-table\na=1\n[a.b.c.d]\n=== overwrite-array-in-parent\n[[parent-table.arr]]\n[parent-table]\nnot-arr = 1\narr = 2\n=== redefine-01\n# Define b as int, and try to use it as a table: error\n[a]\nb = 1\n\n[a.b]\nc = 2\n=== redefine-02\n[t1]\nt2.t3.v = 0\n[t1.t2]\n=== redefine-03\n[t1]\nt2.t3.v = 0\n[t1.t2.t3]\n=== super-twice\n[a.b]\n[a]\n[a]\n=== duplicate-key-07\n[[tbl]]\n[tbl]\n=== duplicate-key-08\n[a]\nb = { c = 2, d = {} }\n[a.b]\nc = 2\n=== duplicate-key-09\n[a]\nfoo=\"bar\"\n[a.b]\nfoo=\"bar\"\n[a]\n=== duplicate-key-010\ncat: duplicate-key-010.toml: No such file or directory\n=== empty-implicit-table\n[naughty..naughty]\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"365a8363-0406-4065-821b-7ed4543381d1","uuid":"d6d2474d-2c11-497f-9836-2147dc919bae","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:19:35.196Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"=== array-implicit\n# This test is a bit tricky. Namely, it wouldn't\n# comply with the TOML spec: \"Each double-bracketed sub-table will belong to \n# the most *recently* defined table element *above* it.\"\n#\n# This is in contrast to the *valid* test, table-array-implicit where\n# `[[albums.songs]]` works by itself, so long as `[[albums]]` isn't declared\n# later. (Although, `[albums]` could be.)\n[[albums.songs]]\nname = \"Glory Days\"\n\n[[albums]]\nname = \"Born in the USA\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-01\n# First a.b.c defines a table: a.b.c = {z=9}\n#\n# Then we define a.b.c.t = \"str\" to add a str to the above table, making it:\n#\n#   a.b.c = {z=9, t=\"...\"}\n#\n# While this makes sense, logically, it was decided this is not valid TOML as\n# it's too confusing/convoluted.\n# \n# See: https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/issues/846\n#      https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/pull/859\n\n[a.b.c]\n  z = 9\n\n[a]\n  b.c.t = \"Using dotted keys to add to [a.b.c] after explicitly defining it above is not allowed\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-02\n# This is the same issue as in injection-1.toml, except that nests one level\n# deeper. See that file for a more complete description.\n\n[a.b.c.d]\n  z = 9\n\n[a]\n  b.c.d.k.t = \"Using dotted keys to add to [a.b.c.d] after explicitly defining it above is not allowed\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-03\n[[a.b]]\n\n[a]\nb.y = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-04\n[dependencies.foo]\nversion = \"0.16\"\n\n[dependencies]\nlibc = \"0.2\"\n\n[dependencies]\nrand = \"0.3.14\"\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-05\na.b.c = 1\na.b = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-06\na = 1\na.b = 2\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-07\na = {k1 = 1, k1.name = \"joe\"}\n=== append-with-dotted-keys-08\n[a.b.c]\nz = 9\n\n[[totally_unrelated]]\nx = 123\n\n[a]\nb.c.t = \"this should NOT be allowed\"\n=== overwrite-with-deep-table\na=1\n[a.b.c.d]\n=== overwrite-array-in-parent\n[[parent-table.arr]]\n[parent-table]\nnot-arr = 1\narr = 2\n=== redefine-01\n# Define b as int, and try to use it as a table: error\n[a]\nb = 1\n\n[a.b]\nc = 2\n=== redefine-02\n[t1]\nt2.t3.v = 0\n[t1.t2]\n=== redefine-03\n[t1]\nt2.t3.v = 0\n[t1.t2.t3]\n=== super-twice\n[a.b]\n[a]\n[a]\n=== duplicate-key-07\n[[tbl]]\n[tbl]\n=== duplicate-key-08\n[a]\nb = { c = 2, d = {} }\n[a.b]\nc = 2\n=== duplicate-key-09\n[a]\nfoo=\"bar\"\n[a.b]\nfoo=\"bar\"\n[a]\n=== duplicate-key-010\ncat: duplicate-key-010.toml: No such file or directory\n=== empty-implicit-table\n[naughty..naughty]","stderr":"\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01J5aLBHzBhcn8GtTXMpbrNn","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

A nested table\n// is a table value; a key/value pair is the tagged map[string]any that value returns.\n// The two dynamic types differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table map[string]any\n\n// key reads a dotted key: one or more key parts joined by '.'. Spaces and tabs around\n// each part are ignored. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key. Table headers are not\n// decoded yet, so a '[' is reported as a syntax error by the caller.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below doc, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(doc table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tcur := doc\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, exists := cur[part]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tsub := table{}\n\t\t\tcur[part] = sub\n\t\t\tcur = sub\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsub, ok := next.(table)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", part)\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = sub\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps for the caller. Values are shared,\n// not copied, because each leaf is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t))\n\tfor k, v := range t {\n\t\tif sub, ok := v.(table); ok {\n\t\t\tout[k] = sub.export()\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":10,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":[" package toml"," ","-// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Table headers are not\n// decoded yet, so a '[' is reported as a syntax error by the caller.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below doc, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(doc table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tcur := doc\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, exists := cur[part]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tsub := table{}\n\t\t\tcur[part] = sub\n\t\t\tcur = sub\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsub, ok := next.(table)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", part)\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = sub\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps for the caller. Values are shared,\n// not copied, because each leaf is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t))\n\tfor k, v := range t {\n\t\tif sub, ok := v.(table); ok {\n\t\t\tout[k] = sub.export()\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":19,"oldLines":8,"newStart":19,"newLines":7,"lines":["   }"," }"," ","-// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key. each table maps to\n// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.\n// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}","originalFile":"// Package toml decodes TOML v1.0.0 documents using only the standard library.\npackage toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"unicode/utf8\"\n)\n\n// ErrSyntax reports a document that TOML v1.0.0 does not allow. Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each top-level key maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string.\n// Only top-level key/value pairs with string, boolean, integer, or float values are decoded so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) document() (table, error) {\n\tdoc := table{}\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn doc, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c := p.src[p.pos]; c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r' {\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.insert(doc, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() ([]string, map[string]any, error) {\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tname := strings.Join(parts, \".\")\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", name)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn parts, value, nil\n}\n\n// value reads one value and returns its tagged model. Strings start with a quote;\n// everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '_'\n}\n\n// isDisallowedControl reports whether c is a control character TOML forbids in\n// strings and comments. Tab is the only control character it allows. Line breaks\n// are excluded here because each caller decides whether a line break is legal.\nfunc isDisallowedControl(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c < 0x20 && c != '\\t' && c != '\\n') || c == 0x7f\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":8,"newStart":14,"newLines":9,"lines":[" var ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")"," "," // Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.","-// Each top-level key maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string.","-// Only top-level key/value pairs with string, boolean, integer, or float values are decoded so far.","+// Each leaf maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string; each table maps to","+// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.","+// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far."," func Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {","   data, err := io.ReadAll(r)","   if err != nil {"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_015nuPHjU8B4BKL1Q923F6oS","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each leaf maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string; each table maps to\n// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.\n// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) document() (table, error) {\n\tdoc := table{}\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn doc, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c := p.src[p.pos]; c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r' {\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.insert(doc, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() ([]string, map[string]any, error) {\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tname := strings.Join(parts, \".\")\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", name)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn parts, value, nil\n}\n\n// value reads one value and returns its tagged model. Strings start with a quote;\n// everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool All Go tests pass with `-race`, and all 24 valid and 62 invalid table cases from toml-test pass.\n\n**The declared suite gate is vacuous as written.** `tables-suite-slice` passes `valid/table/**|invalid/table/**`. toml-test's `-run` takes comma-separated `filepath.Match` globs, not `|` alternation, so the pattern selects zero cases and the run exits 0 with \"0 passed, 0 failed, 884 skipped\". The staged scripts and the criterion are read-only, so I left them alone. I ran the same slice with `'valid/table/*,invalid/table/*'`, which is the real verdict above. The criterion needs fixing on replan.\n\n**What changed** (in `internal/toml`, plus cmd tests):\n- `tables.go` (new): each table carries an origin (implicit, header-defined, or dotted-defined). `[name]` and `[[name]]` headers are parsed here. `[[name]]` builds a `tableArray`, which exports as a JSON array of objects. Sub-tables attach to the most recent element.\n- `keys.go`: the old map-based table type is gone. Dotted keys may extend only dotted-created tables.\n- `toml.go`: `document()` tracks the current scope and dispatches `[` lines to header parsing.\n- `tables_test.go` and `cmd/toml-decoder/tables_test.go` (new): the three declared round-trip and rejection behaviors plus boundary and redefinition cases. They assert on decoded structure and `ErrSyntax`, not message text.\n\n**Choices I made:**\n- I removed the `\"table header\"` case from `TestDecodeRejectsMalformedDocuments` in `toml_test.go`. That case pinned the previous block's \"headers not supported\" stub, and the spec now makes it valid. This was not one of the declared acceptance assertions.\n- A dotted key that walks into a header-implied table (for example, `[x.y.z]`, then `[x]`, then `y.w = 1`) is rejected. The spec says dotted keys may not touch tables that were \"previously created\", and no toml-test case contradicts it.\n\n**Verification:**\n- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `go vet ./...` is clean.\n- `go test -race ./...` passes.\n- The three declared round-trip and rejection assertions, run as written from outside the build directory, all pass.\n- `toml-decoder` was rebuilt by the harness scripts, so the binary changed as well.\n\nRESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- internal/toml/tables.go\n- internal/toml/tables_test.go\n- internal/toml/keys.go\n- internal/toml/toml.go\n- internal/toml/toml_test.go\n- cmd/toml-decoder/tables_test.go\n- toml-decoder\n\nSUMMARY:\nImplemented standard table headers, implicit super-tables, arrays of tables, and the redefinition rules for FEATURE-Parser-Tables. Dotted-key and header definitions are tracked by origin so redefinitions are rejected. Scoped conformance slice, run with a pattern that actually selects cases: valid/table 24 passed / 0 failed; invalid/table 62 passed / 0 failed. The declared pattern `valid/table/**|invalid/table/**` selects zero cases and exits 0, so it proves nothing.\n\nBLOCKERS:\n- `tables-suite-slice` uses `|` as an alternation, which toml-test does not support, so the declared gate runs zero cases and passes vacuously. It needs `valid/table/*,invalid/table/*` on replan. I did not modify the staged script or criterion.\n\n<blueprint-decisions>\n[{\"spec\":\"FEATURE-Parser-Tables.md\",\"severity\":\"Low\",\"subject\":\"Dotted key into a header-implied table\",\"decision\":\"A dotted key that walks into a super-table created implicitly by a header (for example, [x.y.z], then [x], then y.w = 1) is rejected.
